decisions.quote:
In summary, with regard to the original ﬁndings by Southgate et al. (2007), only the FB1
condition of the Southgate/Senju task could be replicated.
decisions.reason: While the abstract states broadly across tasks that original looking patterns could not be replicated, the target-specific verdict in the Discussion explicitly frames the replication of Southgate et al. (2007) as partial, with the FB1 condition replicating on differential looking scores while the FB2 condition and first-saccade measures did not ('the study still did not fully replicate it'). Under the codebook, a target framed by the authors as partly replicating and partly not is coded as mixed.

corrected_value.title: Where will the triangle look for it? Attributing false beliefs to a geometric shape at 17 months

decisions.quote:
Crucially, however, even after adding verbal narration, original ﬁndings could still not
reliably be replicated, particularly in the Surian and Geraci task—much in line with
previous large-scale failed replication attempts of anticipatory looking false belief tasks
(Kulke et al., 2018). A lack of looking patterns in line with false belief processing in the
Surian and Geraci (2012) task may be because the eﬀect is fragile and hence diﬃcult to
measure.
decisions.reason: The paper collects new eye-tracking data to re-test the anticipatory-looking false-belief task of Surian and Geraci (2012) with added verbal narration and concludes that its original findings could not be replicated, making it an omitted replication target with a failed outcome.
